The defaults are suggestions; take another where the tree shows a reason, and say why. The record test pins the names the record uses. (1) How the browser bar colour reaches the page from the first paint. Default: a meta of the module's own. The script, when the stored choice is Light or Dark, creates one `` with no media attribute, content #1a2744 (Light) or #0b1220 (Dark), marks it as its own (for example a data attribute) and puts it first in the head; browsers use the first theme-color meta that has no media or whose media matches, so it wins over index.html's two, which stay as they are, and with System the script adds nothing and the two media metas follow the device as today. createColorScheme owns the same element afterwards: when the choice changes it updates the element's content, adds it for Light or Dark, removes it for System, never makes two, and does nothing when newLook is off (enabled false) or when it is handed no way to reach the head. The colours are two exported constants in src/lib/colorScheme.ts, shared by the script and the module, and test/unit/theme-color.test.ts reads index.html and requires its two metas to hold the same two values (so the three places cannot drift). The page's head is reached the way the module already reaches the root: the caller (src/hooks/useColorScheme.ts) hands in a function or object, and the module stays free of browser globals. The script keeps the class and data-look work first and puts the theme work in a try of its own, so a head that cannot be reached never costs the dark class. Alternative if the builder finds a blocker: a second small script injected at the end of the head (after the metas exist) that edits the existing two; if that is chosen, test/unit/prepaint-gate.test.ts's 'script first in the head' and 'one script' cases must be moved with the reason. The manifest's acceptance reads 'both theme-color metas carry that look's colour'; with the default the page's effective colour is what is pinned (see the test below), and the record says so.
